chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Ali ibn Abdul-Aziz, from Murad ibn Kharajat, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for me, so whenever it is the day of Friday, and the sun is from the east to the west by its measure, during the time of the 'Asr prayer, I pray six rak'at. So when the day swells, I pray six. So when the sun dips or declines, I pray two rak'at, then I pray the Dhuhr prayer, then I pray six after it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific voluntary prayer routine of Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) on Friday afternoons?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophet's tradition (Sunnah) of Friday prayers by detailing Imam al-Sadiq’s specific personal practice, which serves as a model for the recommended *Salat al-Friday* (Prayer of Friday). The narration emphasizes the spiritual significance of specific solar timings—such as the sun's rise, zenith, and decline—to structure voluntary worship, reinforcing the day's sanctity in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the importance of adhering to precise temporal markers for voluntary acts of devotion, linking celestial movements with spiritual discipline.
